# CodeBlock

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

typography and layout · tier 2 · beta · renders on the server, with only its interactive part in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For code a reader copies or studies: a file, a command, a snippet. It is a `<pre><code>` on the
server; the only script is the copy button, and `showCopy={false}` drops that too.

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from 'topclassui/code-block'
```

```tsx
<CodeBlock lang="tsx" title="page.tsx">
  {`export default async function Page() {
  const invoices = await getInvoices()
  return <InvoiceTable items={invoices} />
}`}
</CodeBlock>
```

**The code is `children`, a string.** Pass a template literal: every space and line break is kept,
and that string is what the button copies.

**Code reads left to right in every page.** The `<pre>` is always `dir="ltr"` and
`translate="no"`. The header keeps the page's direction, so in Arabic the button sits on the left,
at the inline end; the title is `dir="auto"`.

**`title`** names the block: the code becomes a `region` named by it, and the button reads
"Copy page.tsx", so five blocks on a page are five different buttons. Without a title the button
reads "Copy" and there is no header unless the button is shown.

**`lang`** is written as `data-lang` and nothing else. No highlighter is built in. To colour the
code, make the nodes yourself (a highlighter at build time, or your own async Server Component) and
pass them as `highlighted`: they are rendered in place of the text, and the button still copies
`children`. Their colours are yours to check against the block's surface.

**The surface** is `neutral-solid` with `neutral-on-solid` text: dark in Light and Ocean, light in
Dark, as drawn. Both focus rings take the text colour of the block.

**A long line scrolls** inside the `<pre>`, which is a tab stop so a keyboard can scroll it (the
server cannot know whether a line overflows). `wrap` breaks long lines instead, and then the `<pre>`
is no tab stop.

**The copy button** needs a secure context (`https` or `localhost`). Elsewhere, or when the browser
refuses, it says "Could not copy" and keeps its icon. After a copy the icon turns to a tick and a
hidden status says "Copied"; both clear after 2 seconds. The name of the button never changes.

**Labels.** In a Server Component pass `{...getLabels(locale)}`: the button's three words come from
`labels.common` (`copy`, `copied`, `copyFailed`) through props, with or without a provider.

| What the platform gives | How CodeBlock uses it |
|---|---|
| `<pre>` keeps every space and line break | the code, unchanged |
| `navigator.clipboard.writeText` after a press, in a secure context | the copy; `undefined` elsewhere, which reads as a failure |
| `role="status"` is a polite live region | "Copied" or "Could not copy", once per press |

### Not built

A highlighter of any kind (Shiki was asked about: choice 12), a syntax palette, line numbers,
highlighted lines, `maxLines`, a `theme` prop, a language badge, a fixed dark surface (choice 13), a
shared CopyButton component (choice 14), a download button, `size`.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from 'topclassui/code-block'
```

## Props

Required: `children`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | **yes** | `string` | - | The code, as a template literal: every space and line break is kept, and this is what the button copies. |
| `highlighted` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The same code as nodes the caller coloured, for example with a highlighter at build time. Rendered in place of children. |
| `labels` | no | `Labels` | - | The built-in strings of the copy button. Defaults to English; pass `getLabels(locale).labels` for another. |
| `lang` | no | `string` | - | The language, written as data-lang for a stylesheet or a script to read. Nothing here colours it. |
| `locale` | no | `string` | - | Accepted so `{...getLabels(locale)}` spreads cleanly. Nothing here formats a number, so it is not used and never reaches the element. |
| `showCopy` | no | `boolean` | `true` | Shows a button in the header that copies the code: the one part that runs in the browser. |
| `title` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The file name in the header. It names the code region and the copy button. |
| `wrap` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Breaks a long line instead of scrolling it sideways; the code is then no tab stop. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
